findings.source: VRF.sol / VRFCoordinatorV2Plus: abi.encodePacked / abi.encode of uint256[2] points (pk, gamma, uWitness, cGammaWitness, sHashWitness) for hashToCurve, scalarFromCurvePoints and the request id
findings.issue: The ABI encoding of a static uint256[2] memory array, a copy of exactly two words, is printed as a 5-line loop with a constant bound of 2, twelve times.
findings.rule: A word-copy loop with a constant trip count n (i = 0; while i < n: mem[d + 32i] = mem[s + 32i]) is the copy line mem[d len 32n] = mem[s len 32n] (or n assignments for small n).

findings.source: VRFCoordinatorV2Plus.sol:626 isTargetRegistered: for (i < s_migrationTargets.length) if (s_migrationTargets[i] == target) return true; return false;
findings.issue: The inequality s_migrationTargets[s] != _to is printed as a non-zero difference, the element as raw stor[sha3(19) + s] although the same array prints as stor19[idx] in the other functions, and the slot hash is recomputed in every iteration.
findings.rule: A difference used only as a condition is an inequality (x - y != 0 is x != y); stor[sha3(S) + i] is element i of the array at slot S; a pure expression (sha3 of constants) is loop-invariant.

notes: Test helper contract (ExposedVRFCoordinatorV2Plus). Source loops (12, all whiles): isTargetRegistered (131, 180, 1185: header is the 'not found' test, exit to the normal path, correct), deregisterMigratableCoordinator (293), deregisterProvingKey (387), getActiveSubscriptionIds (468), pendingRequestExists' nested loops (578/586 and copies in removeConsumer/cancel paths), removeConsumer (818), deleteSubscription (891, 1074), migrate's consumer loop (1329/1431), fulfillRandomWords' numWords loop (2646), VRF.fieldHash's 'while (x_ >= FIELD_SIZE)' (1782/1848, 2383/2449) and hashToCurve's 'while (!isOnCurve(rv))' shown readably as 'while addmod(mulmod(...), 7, ...) != mulmod(...)' (1839, 2440). Implicit whiles: 10 rotated storage-to-memory copies of the consumers array (P3), the uint256[2] copies (finding) and other memory copies (P7). The two fulfillRandomWords variants (602 and 787 lines) were reviewed by structure, the rest by reading; faithful. The consumer array of a subscription is raw stor[s + sha3(sha3(_param1, 5) + 2)] (array inside a struct of a mapping, see c00050's finding on struct-held collections).
summary: Faithful text in which all 12 source loops, including the VRF curve loops, are found and readable; minor issues are constant 2-word copies printed as loops, rotated storage copies and a few raw storage expressions.
